summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-03 (window Sept. 27–Oct. 3): I found no candidate that meets every rule. The search budget ran out partway through the scan. Most leads I turned up were dated after the scan date (Calaveras, Oxford County, Aurora rail district, Floyd County, Tuscarora Township). Others were already published (Wayne County, the Trump AI pledge typo, Maricopa ballots). The rest fell before the window or had only one accepted source. The closest lead was MARTA's $620,000 overtime overpayment, but Atlanta News First reported it on Sept. 25, before the window opened. Submitting no candidates for this side. Genius: Scan for 2026-10-03, genius side. The best-sourced lead is the record trip by NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 on Oct. 1: 7 hours 55 minutes from launch at Cape Canaveral to docking at the ISS, the fastest ever by a U.S. spacecraft. It is backed by Space.com, CBS News and NASA's own blog. I also have three MacArthur Fellows, all announced Sept. 29, which is inside the window. I chose them because their states haven't appeared recently: Marika Holland of NSF NCAR in Boulder, CO (NCAR release, MacArthur page and the Boston Globe/NYT list), public artist Chip Thomas of Flagstaff, AZ (Boston Globe and his MacArthur profile), and Felipe De Brigard of Duke (WFAE, Duke Today and the Boston Globe). Note that Guan (Oct. 4) and Spradley (Sept. 30) are also MacArthur stories, so the three fellows are mainly alternates. I ran out of searches before finding a fresh research result led from the US that falls inside the window. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published. The verified genius story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 docks at the space station 7 hours 55 minutes after launch, a U.S. record
candidates.reason: fails the schema: ✖ summary is longer than four sentences

candidates.headline: NSF NCAR climate scientist Marika Holland of Boulder is named a 2026 MacArthur Fellow
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Flagstaff public artist Chip Thomas, known for murals on the Navajo Nation, is named a MacArthur Fellow
Duke memory researcher Felipe De Brigard is named a 2026 MacArthur Fellow
MARTA sues former cleaner after a clerical error paid $620,000 in unearned overtime
candidates.reason: Too old for this scan. Atlanta News First first reported it on Sept. 25 and WSB-TV followed on Sept. 28. The overpayment was in April and the lawsuit was filed before the Sept. 27–Oct. 3 window.

candidates.headline: Maricopa County property tax bills arrive after the Oct. 1 due date
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source was found (AZFamily, Sept. 30); the other coverage (ABC15, YouTube) isn't accepted. This is a mailing delay the treasurer attributes to levy changes and a new computer system, not a clear blunder, and Maricopa County was already used on Oct. 6.

candidates.headline: TSA finds a knife hidden inside a baseball bat-shaped flashlight at Tampa International Airport
candidates.reason: The discovery happened earlier in September, before the window. It rests on a TSA release plus one WKMG write-up, and the passenger is unnamed with no city.

candidates.headline: Calaveras County reprints voter pamphlets after vendor prints June candidate statements
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 4, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Maine 'packaging error' sends wrong ballots to some Oxford County voters
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 7, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Rail district miscommunication blamed for wrong ballots sent to 800,000 Aurora-area voters
candidates.reason: Reported around Oct. 8, after the scan date. The only source found (Sentinel Colorado) isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Tuscarora Township, Mich., clerk apologizes for mailing absentee ballots late
candidates.reason: The Votebeat report is dated Oct. 9, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: City of Houston error allowed demolition of a protected historic home in Independence Heights
Knicks pause ticket sales after prices were mistakenly set too high
candidates.reason: Reported in mid-September, outside the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: Suspected second-generation planet solves a Hubble cold case
candidates.reason: Not US-led: the lead author is at the University of Warwick in the UK. NASA's release is also dated Oct. 5, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: NASA's X-59 completes a record six flights in one week and reaches Mach 1.53
candidates.reason: The flights took place Sept. 22–25, before the window. The only source is NASA's own blog (Oct. 2), with no accepted news page, and it is an internal test-program record.

candidates.headline: Oregon State nanoparticle therapy fights lung cancer and muscle wasting in mice
candidates.reason: A mouse study. The only accepted page is ScienceDaily, dated Oct. 5 (after the scan date), and the journal publication date is unconfirmed.

candidates.headline: Memorial Sloan Kettering finds MEK drives T-cell exhaustion
candidates.reason: An animal study in Immunity, from an earlier issue. The ScienceDaily page is dated Oct. 5, after the scan date, and no second source was found.

candidates.headline: NPR coverage of 2026 MacArthur Fellows
candidates.reason: The NPR pages cannot be fetched (url not allowed), so the Boston Globe list and local or official pages were used instead.
